body:
## Office fitout Newcastle: start with a brief you can price

Planning an office fitout in Newcastle starts with three questions: will the premises support the way your team works, what must be included in the whole project budget, and what evidence is needed before you can occupy? A good-looking concept alone does not answer them.

This guide is for a business moving into a Newcastle office or refurbishing an existing workplace. It helps you organise the client decisions before requesting proposals. For YOS's management scope, see [office fitout project management in Newcastle](/office-fitout).

**Take the working pack:** [Download the Office FitOut Project Brief & Quote Comparison Checklist (PDF)](/guides/fitout-project-checklist.pdf). It includes 12 checks, a premises brief, a three-proposal comparison sheet and a decision and handover register. Print it or annotate it in your PDF app. No email is required to read it.

## Choose the project you actually need

Separate a furniture order, an office refurbishment and a fitout involving building works. They can overlap, but the quote needs to show where each scope begins and ends.

| Starting point | First decision | Information to gather |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing office, furniture no longer suits | Can a revised layout and furniture solve the problem? | Current plan, retained items, workstation tasks and access |
| Occupied workplace needs refurbishment | Can work be staged without compromising operations? | Affected rooms, restricted hours, IT changeovers and temporary work areas |
| New premises or substantial changes | Is the space suitable for the proposed use and works? | Existing condition, landlord requirements and specialist advice |

A furniture-only project can start with our [Newcastle office furniture buying guide](/blog/office-furniture-newcastle). A broader fitout needs the premises, building services, furniture and move coordinated against one brief.

## 1. Test the Newcastle premises before committing

Record the actual address and floor, the area you expect to use and whether the space is vacant or occupied. Ask for available plans, photos, existing fitout information and landlord works. Have the relevant specialists verify dimensions and service capacities that affect the proposal.

For an upper-floor office in the CBD or Honeysuckle, ask the building manager about goods-lift dimensions, loading arrangements, booked delivery windows, after-hours access and waste removal. These are checks for your building, not claims that every Newcastle site has the same restrictions. For an older tenancy, ask your appointed advisers what investigations are needed before disturbing existing materials or changing the layout.

Do not assume a Newcastle postal address identifies the consent authority. Confirm the property's council area and applicable requirements. Your solicitor should review lease obligations; your appointed planning adviser or certifier should assess the actual proposal. A landlord's agreement and statutory approvals are separate questions.

## 2. Write the workplace brief around activities

Headcount is useful, but it is not the whole layout. Record current staff, expected peak attendance, visitors, confidential conversations, video meetings, storage, accessible use and work that needs concentration. Identify what is not working today and rank the changes.

A brief might say: “We need space for private calls without taking the only meeting room out of use.” That is more helpful than prescribing a particular product before the layout and services have been checked. Test proposed furniture dimensions against movement, door operation, storage access and the tasks people perform.

Divide the brief into **essential for opening**, **useful if affordable**, and **a later stage**. Assign one person to approve trade-offs. This gives designers, suppliers and contractors a common basis for discussing options.

## 3. Build a whole-project budget

An office fitout cost per square metre can hide very different inclusions. Start with a scope and record the status of each allowance: confirmed quote, provisional allowance, excluded, or still unpriced. Do not add a supplier's furniture total to a works quote without checking whether the same items are already included.

| Budget line | Clarification to request |
| --- | --- |
| Professional inputs | Who allows for design, surveys, consultants, certifier and client-side management? |
| Landlord and existing premises | What is retained, removed, repaired or provided separately? |
| Building works and services | Which drawings, quantities, specifications and allowances support the price? |
| Furniture, IT and security | Who supplies, installs, connects, tests and removes packaging? |
| Transition and disruption | Have moving, staged work and existing-lease exit tasks been allowed for? |
| Risk and cash flow | Are GST treatment, contingency, payment milestones and exclusions clear? |

Use our [Newcastle fitout budget guide](/blog/commercial-fitout-cost-newcastle-2026) for the cost workstreams and the [indicative FitOut estimator](/resources/fitout-estimator) as a conversation starter. Neither replaces project-specific quotations or professional assessment.

## 4. Confirm approval responsibilities before fixing dates

Approval requirements depend on the proposed use, the actual works, the premises and applicable controls. Some work may qualify for an exempt pathway; other proposals may need further assessment. Avoid treating “internal works” or “already an office” as a universal answer.

Ask the appointed adviser to record the proposed pathway, information required, responsible party and prerequisites for starting work and occupation. City of Newcastle publishes building, fire-safety and certification guidance; NSW Planning Portal explains conditional change-of-use pathways. Use those official resources to frame questions for the project team, rather than self-certifying the project from a checklist.

Landlord conditions, building management rules and contractor access also need owners and dates in the programme. A target opening date remains an assumption until the dependencies have been checked.

## 5. Compare quotes using one scope revision

Send each provider the same brief, drawings and specification revision. Then compare the scope behind the number. The PDF's comparison sheet has columns for three proposals and a fourth for the clarification or decision needed.

Check quantities, named products or performance specifications, alternatives, provisional sums, exclusions, delivery, installation, access assumptions, quote validity and programme dependencies. Mark an unanswered item **unconfirmed**, not zero. Ask for a revised written proposal when a clarification materially changes the scope.

For example, one furniture offer might include assembly and packaging removal while another is delivery only. That is a scope difference to resolve before comparing totals. The same principle applies to works, consultant inputs and testing. Record who approves any substitution before it is ordered.

## 6. Work backwards from occupation

Build a dependency sequence instead of choosing an arbitrary number of weeks. The usual questions are: when can the brief be approved, when are design and landlord decisions needed, what approvals apply, when can appointed contractors access the site, and which furniture or equipment must arrive before the team moves?

If the office stays open, identify work zones, staff access, noisy or dusty work, meeting-room availability and IT downtime with the appointed project team. Include an alternative if a critical delivery or decision moves. Do not promise a standard completion period without a site-specific programme.

## The 12-point office fitout checklist

1. Define the workplace outcome and essential opening-day activities.
2. Record the site, plans, condition and information requiring verification.
3. Name the client decision maker, landlord contact and appointed specialists.
4. Issue one written scope with a revision date.
5. Separate confirmed prices, allowances and unpriced items.
6. Compare the whole budget, including furniture, IT and transition.
7. Confirm approval and occupation dependencies with the responsible advisers.
8. Plan business continuity, site access and changeovers.
9. Coordinate furniture dimensions, layout, power and data before ordering.
10. Verify contractor and supplier availability for this project.
11. Agree handover evidence, testing, documentation and the defects process.
12. Record the next decision, its owner and the date it is needed.

[Use the printable checklist and worksheets](/guides/fitout-project-checklist.pdf). Keep a dated copy with the brief so changes remain visible.

## What must be ready at handover?

A completed-looking office still needs operational checks. Agree who confirms required approvals, services testing, keys and access, IT readiness, furniture completion, instructions, warranties and outstanding defects. Give each open item an owner and agreed response date. Your appointed certifier and specialists determine the evidence required for their scope.

Our [office fitout handover guide](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist) goes deeper into the final inspection and first working day. Set those expectations at the start of procurement.

## Common questions about a Newcastle office fitout

### Does an office fitout include furniture?

Only if it is included in the agreed scope. Separate the building works, furniture, technology, delivery and installation so each item has an owner and is neither omitted nor counted twice.

### How much does an office fitout in Newcastle cost?

There is no dependable project price without the premises condition, quantities, design, services, approvals, furniture and programme. Ask for a scope-based budget and clarify assumptions before comparing quotations.

### Can we refurbish while the business remains open?

It may be possible, depending on the work and site. The appointed team needs to assess safe separation, access, staging and disruption. Include the cost and operational implications when comparing that option with moving out temporarily.

### Can YOS construct the fitout?

YOS acts as your client-side project manager, not the builder or head contractor. We can coordinate the brief, budget, consultants, procurement, decisions and handover within an agreed management scope. Appropriately appointed and licensed contractors perform the construction and trade work.

## Turn the checklist into your next decision

You do not need a finished design to start a useful conversation. Bring the site suburb, project stage, what needs changing, whether the business must stay open, and your target date. Mark unknowns clearly.

[Discuss your Newcastle office fitout with YOS](/office-fitout#fitout-enquiry). If you are still comparing premises, connect the workplace brief with [tenant representation](/tenant-rep) before making the property commitment.
